expectedRealization.rationale: Quota concentration is an upstream cost state that can affect packaging-paper margins over multiple procurement/inventory cycles; Q2/H1 results and subsequent quota/price data are observable within 60d.

acceptableExpressionSet.rationale: Shanying had a large share of import-waste-paper quota, an estimated >RMB500/t imported-vs-domestic fiber cost gap, Q1 revenue +60.6% and profit +39.9%, and a ~7x 2018E PE. The company was mechanically early-turning while the broader wastepaper basket remained weak over 60d.

changeHypothesis.summary: Tighter imported-waste-paper standards and sharply lower national quota volumes created an industry-wide recycled-fiber shortage, but quota became concentrated in leaders. For quota-rich Shanying, imported-fiber access became a relative raw-material cost advantage before sector-wide paper margins and stock prices fully reflected the difference.
changeHypothesis.persistenceReason: Import standards and quota concentration are regulatory/operational states that can persist across multiple procurement cycles; the advantage lasts while imported fiber remains cheaper and quota access stays concentrated.
disconfirmingEvidence: Industry-wide domestic waste-paper prices were rising sharply and could still pressure all packaging-paper producers.
Shanying Q1 operating cash flow remained slightly negative despite large improvement.
The broader paper basket was weak over 60d, so the thesis requires company-specific divergence rather than sector momentum.

evidenceLedger.supportsClaim: Imported-waste-paper standards tightened and made access more compliance-sensitive.
National quota fell sharply while Shanying held a material share.
Quota concentration created a relative raw-material cost advantage for leaders.
Imported waste paper was estimated >RMB500/t cheaper than domestic waste paper and Shanying had large quota access.
Shanying had already realized strong Q1 revenue/profit growth.
Forward valuation was low relative to sector while forecast earnings remained positive.
Independent research corroborated quota concentration, low valuation and leader cost advantage.
A lower-quota peer explicitly reported gross-margin pressure from higher-priced domestic waste paper.
Broad paper price regime was neutral while Shanying showed an early-turn pattern.
